where: Section 2 (curl and the paddle wheel), sentence about the j component
problem: The text says the j component is ∂F₁/∂z − ∂F₃/∂x "with the x-derivative of F₁ first". ∂F₁/∂z is F₁ differentiated with respect to z, not x. A student who follows this sentence will differentiate F₁ with respect to the wrong variable.
fix: Write: "the j component runs the other way: it is ∂F₁/∂z − ∂F₃/∂x, the term containing F₁ first and differentiated with respect to z."

where: Section 3 (product rules and the three identities)
problem: The text says "Two identities are exam favourites" and then lists three bullets, one of which (div(∇φ) = ∇²φ) is a definition of the Laplacian rather than a prove-that identity. The count does not match what follows.
fix: Say "Two identities are exam favourites and are always worded prove that", list div(curl F) = 0 and curl(∇φ) = 0, then introduce the Laplacian in a separate sentence: "The divergence of a gradient defines the Laplacian: div(∇φ) = ∇²φ = ...".
